The angles ${30}^{∘}$ and ${60}^{∘}$ are special, and their trigonometric ratios have the  values

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡{30}^{∘}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2},\,\operatorname{sin}⁡{60}^{∘}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡{30}^{∘}-\operatorname{sin}⁡{60}^{∘} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} & = \\ 0 & .\end{aligned}
$$
